pr_title: iptables: added choices in match_set_flags option
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY

  match_set_flags option

Fixes: #81281

Signed-off-by: Abhijeet Kasurde <akasurde@redhat.com>

- Bugfix Pull Request

issue_context.title: Iptables module doesn't support all valid options
issue_context.body:
### Summary

ansible/lib/ansible/modules/iptables.py doesn't have all supported options for match_set_flags dist needs changing from 

            match_set_flags=dict(type='str', choices=['src', 'dst', 'src,dst', 'dst,src']),

to 

            match_set_flags=dict(type='str', choices=['src', 'dst', 'src,dst', 'dst,src', 'dst,dst, 'src,src']),

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

iptables

review_comments: To have separate tests in the report, use `@pytest.mark.parametrize`. Otherwise, a failure in one iteration will prevent others from even starting.
Can we use `pytest.mark.parametrize` in `unittest` as these tests are written in `unittest`?

@Akasurde it depends on whether we inherit from `unittest.TestCase`. If yes ­— it limits the use of some of the pytest features, though, there's hacks like autouse fixtures and parameterizing them. If not — all pytest features use for methods in regular classes (though, I do prefer plain functions over methods because I dislike unnecessary scoping/nesting).

That said, `unittest` has a feature to display subtests. You just have to use something like `with self.subTest(id='a param')` in the loop and every case will show up in the test report as a separate entry. (clarify the syntax in the docs, plz!)
